summary_en: Hokuriku Electric Industry amended its November 10 disclosure regarding BCJ-116's public tender offer. The revision adds that BCJ-116 concluded a share application agreement with Hokuriku Bank (301,407 shares, 3.84% of outstanding shares, ranked 5th largest shareholder) on November 17, 2026, in addition to the previously disclosed four shareholders totaling 1,495,965 shares.
title_en: Notice of Partial Correction to "Notice of Opinions in Support and Recommendation to Apply for Public Tender Offer for Our Shares by BCJ-116 Corporation"
translation_en_brief:
On November 20, 2026, Hokuriku Electric Industry issued a correction notice to its November 10 press release regarding BCJ-116's public tender offer for its shares. The principal correction concerns the addition of Hokuriku Bank to the list of shareholders who have committed to tendering their shares.

According to the corrected disclosure, on November 17, 2026, BCJ-116 concluded a share application agreement with Hokuriku Bank covering 301,407 shares, representing 3.84% of outstanding shares (excluding treasury stock) and ranking as the fifth-largest shareholder as of March 31, 2026. This agreement obligates Hokuriku Bank to tender these shares in the public offer. The November 10 disclosure had already included four other major shareholders: Fellowtech (1,048,800 shares, 13.36%, ranked 1st), Hokuriku Bank (158,365 shares, 2.02%, ranked 6th), Maeda Corporation (149,000 shares, 1.90%, ranked 7th), and Toyama Bank (139,800 shares, 1.78%, ranked 8th), which together committed to tender 1,495,965 shares. With the addition of Hokuriku Bank's agreement, the total committed shares increased by 301,407 shares to approximately 1.8 million shares or roughly 23% of outstanding shares.

The November 17 agreement between BCJ-116 and Hokuriku Bank includes lock-up provisions restricting Hokuriku Bank's ability to sell, pledge, or otherwise dispose of the tendered shares, or acquire additional company shares, until settlement. The agreement also includes a matching rights clause allowing Hokuriku Bank to terminate the agreement and accept a superior proposal exceeding the tender price by 5% or more, provided that Hokuriku Bank first gives BCJ-116 an opportunity to match such offer. These terms are consistent with standard public tender offer protections.
